slice: Pre-code challenge of the Match Deck shortlist and first-conversation experience. Decide how Werkles should prefer useful variety without padding the deck with weak or cloned people, and how the page should explain a short honest result.
sharedContext: Ben caught the Foreman implementing beyond actual cousin receipts. Product edits are paused until this mission returns and is assimilated.

The rendered owner walkthrough previously showed Ava and Bo as different people but effectively the same Backer archetype: retired contractors with the same offers, asks, proof gap, and first-test answer.

The current unreviewed local candidate prefers distinct lane/role/offer/ask contribution signatures after preserving the strongest scored result, never admits a zero-reason candidate, and can return only two honest profiles instead of padding to three.
Current rendered candidate result is only two people and both are in Virginia. Geographic repetition now compounds the thin-deck problem even if the profiles are not exact clones.

Ben's live walkthrough exposed three offered conversation prompts: 'How could Chair space help this project?', 'How would we clear up Funds not verified?', and 'Which part of the day-to-day work would you test first?' These are the actual quality evidence, not hypothetical placeholder copy.

A fourth live prompt is 'What would you need from me around Ownership?' It confirms the generator is exposing category labels as awkward pseudo-tailoring rather than reasoning about this member and this candidate.

The current signed-in header violates Ben's standing navigation rule: it replaces the standard public navigation with member links. Required behavior is the standard Werkles header remaining visible, with a second stable member-navigation row locked beneath it after sign-in.

The product question is not merely whether two honest profiles beat three with one clone. It is whether the engine has enough grounded information to offer two genuinely useful people and person-specific conversations at all, and how to fail usefully when it does not.

Existing controlling rulings require one causal evaluator, path-specific reasons, authoritative suppressions, stable IDs, provenance-aware interpretations, and separate business readiness from member-match eligibility.

Werkles culture must match interests, temperament, goals, and complementary contributions before money; Backers are not ranked by account value. The Deck is a possibility set, not a verdict or introduction.
No cousin is being asked to implement. Return independent product, UX, trust, or research judgment for one bounded repair packet.
liveStrings: A shortlist is a beginning, not a verdict.
What to test before relying on this fit
Nothing is sent, saved, or introduced by this practice conversation.
knownGaps: The current candidate has automated local proof but no actual-CBCC review receipt.
Synthetic profile fields are bounded and cannot support invented biography, chemistry, availability, or willingness.
The current deterministic engine has limited temperament/personality evidence; it must not pretend otherwise.
Two honest results can look sparse unless the page explains why Werkles withheld weaker repeats and offers a useful next action; two geographically similar results may still be poor variety.
Current conversation prompts appear assembled from raw labels such as Chair space and Funds not verified rather than interpreted into an ordinary, decision-bearing question.
The current header swaps public and member navigation instead of composing both layers, which makes location and site identity less stable after sign-in.
No real member contact, introduction, provider call, account write, payment, or production matching is in scope.
